core_obligations: Choose the factorization and use base change stability to reduce to f^*[Y] = i^!(g^*[Y]) on an integral Y (proof lines 13555-13565).

Assume f flat of relative dimension r and g smooth of relative dimension t, compute f^*[Y] and g^*[Y] as fundamental classes, and use the codimension of the regular immersion i to conclude (proof lines 13565-13572).
proof_roadmap: Factorization and reduction to an integral base (proof lines 13555-13565).
Relative dimensions and the fundamental class computation (proof lines 13565-13572).
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a local complete intersection morphism of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta), if the Gysin map exists for f and f is flat, the lemma asserts that f^! equals the bivariant class of flat pullback of Lemma labelled lemma-flat-pullback-bivariant (statement lines 13546-13553). The proof chooses a factorization f = g o i with i : X -> P an immersion and g : P -> Y smooth, and observes that base change along any Y' -> Y locally of finite type preserves the assumptions, by Morphisms, Lemmas labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-smooth and morphisms-lemma-base-change-syntomic and More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-flat-lci, so by Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero it suffices to prove f^*[Y] = i^!(g^*[Y]) for Y integral (proof lines 13555-13569). Setting n = dim_delta(Y) and decomposing into connected components, one may assume f is flat of relative dimension r and g is smooth of relative dimension t, so f^*[Y] = [X]_{n+s} and g^*[Y] = [P]_{n+t}, while i is a regular immersion of codimension t - s and hence i^![P]_{n+t} = [X]_{n+s} by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-fundamental (proof lines 13565-13572). Reducing to the test on an integral base and then reading the codimension off the relative dimensions is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
